name: Laurus Labs Ltd.
business_summary: Hyderabad-based API, formulations and CDMO company. Segments (model knowledge, verify): Generics (ARV APIs/finished doses, oncology, cardio) ~55-60%, Laurus Synthesis (CDMO/ contract development, ~20-25% and rising fast), Laurus Bio (enzymes/ biologics CDMO, ~5%). Export-heavy (~75-80% of revenue: US, Europe, Africa/Asia ARV tenders). Q2 FY27: revenue Rs 2,206 cr (+33% YoY), EBITDA Rs 750 cr (34%), PAT Rs 436 cr (+126%); CDMO surge. Bought 60% of Canadian oligonucleotide biotech Galenvs Sciences and SI&C Resins (total ~Rs 64 cr, 2026-10-29/11-02) and invested Rs 107.8 cr in KRKA Pharma via rights issue (2026-10-16). Management guides 30%+ EBITDA margin with ~Rs 3,000 cr capex (Trade Brains 2026-11-03). Mcap Rs 1.25 lakh cr, P/E 93, stock +136% in 12m.

revenue_mix.segment: Generics (ARV, oncology, cardio APIs and FDFs)

exposures.mechanism: CDMO growth is the stock's key driver: orders from Western innovators diversifying away from China (BIOSECURE-style policies). CDMO ~32% of Rs 8,000 cr revenue growing ~50%+; each +1 theme unit adds ~10pp to CDMO growth = +3pp group sales at ~35% incremental EBITDA vs 30% base -> +3.5% EBITDA first year, compounded by order visibility to +15% EBITDA over 3 yrs; EV/MCap 1.03, persistence 1.0 -> +6.0. Nuvama sees 24% upside on CDMO shift (ET 2026-10-16).

evidence.note: Laurus shifts gears as CDMO emerges as key growth driver (ET 2026-10-16)

exposures.mechanism: Decoupling steers US innovator outsourcing from Chinese CDMOs to Indian ones. +1 unit -> same direction as T_CHINA_PLUS_ONE but narrower (US only) -> +3.0 (not additive with T_CHINA_PLUS_ONE; the assembler should treat overlap).

Chinese API/intermediate price cuts +15%: hits Laurus's commoditised ARV/API prices (Generics ~55% of sales; China competes in intermediates). 5% price cut on 25% of sales = -1.3% revenue at 100% drop-through = -4.2% EBITDA at 30% OPM; partly offset by cheaper intermediates (RM 45% of costs, 10% share China, -1.5% cost = +2%) -> net -2% EBITDA; EV/MCap 1.03, persistence 0.5 -> -1.0; with multiple risk -1.5.

evidence.note: Q2 margin 34% shows pricing intact; risk is asymmetric

exposures.mechanism: ~85% of revenue USD/EUR-linked (exports + CDMO contracts), imported RM ~25% of costs (≈19% of sales): net 66% x 3% = +2% of sales; at 34% OPM = +5.8% EBITDA; ~50% hedged -> +2.9%; plus operating leverage; EV/MCap 1.03, persistence 0.5 -> +1.5; for a 93x P/E stock the earnings-revision effect is magnified x2.5 -> +4.0. Empirical +2.46 (t=1.3) lower.

evidence.note: Q2 FY27 EBITDA margin 34.5% (Investing.com 2026-10-29); INR -1.9% in 1m

exposures.mechanism: APIs are historically exempt; CDMO exports of branded-drug intermediates sit in a grey area now that branded drugs face 100% tariffs from 2026-09-29 (India's speciality drugs exempt). Customers may shift to US-based supply (reshoring) - CDMO order risk. 15% probability x -10% -> -1.5.

evidence.note: US 100% branded pharma tariff; India speciality exemption (Business Standard 2026-09-29)

exposures.mechanism: Concentrated in a few Visakhapatnam / Anakapalli sites feeding CDMO and generics; an OAI hits CDMO onboarding and customer audits. 15% probability x -25% equity (concentration + 93x P/E) -> -4.0.

evidence.note: Large, concentrated capex: Rs 3,000 cr (Trade Brains 2026-11-03)

exposures.mechanism: Net debt ~Rs 3,000 cr (interest Rs 44 cr/qtr = Rs 176 cr/yr on ~Rs 2,200 cr+ capex capitalised); +25bp = Rs 5 cr = 0.2% EBITDA; discount-rate on 93x P/E dominates: duration ~20 yrs -> -2.0 + funding -> -1.8 net of persistence.

evidence.note: Interest Rs 44 cr in Sep-26 quarter (screener.in)

exposures.mechanism: Generic formulations (US, FDF) ~15% of sales; +5pp erosion -> -0.75% sales -> -2.5% EBITDA, persistence 0.5, EV/MCap 1.03 -> -1.3 (less given API/CDMO mix) -> -1.0.

Peptide/oligonucleotide CDMO (Galenvs acquisition, GLP-1 peptide APIs) could address obesity-drug supply; model knowledge only - option value; +1 unit -> +1.5.
